newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Shindongbang buys 6.74 pct Midopa stake.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Shindongbang buys 6.74 pct Midopa stake.

text.p: South Korea's Shindongbang Corp and its joint-venture Dongbang Peregrine Securities bought a combined 6.74 percent stake in Midopa Department Store in a bid to participate in management of the retailer, a Shindongbang spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We reported our share holdings to the Exchange to comply with securities regulations," the spokesman said.
Under securities rules, related individuals or companies holding more than five percent stake in another listed firm must report their holdings to the Exchange.
He said Shindongbang kept a 4.76 percent stake in Midopa and Dongbang Peregrine kept 1.98 percent.
Shindongbang is a major South Korean shareholder of the joint venture brokerage with a 39 percent stake.
Midopa became the target of the country's first major hostile takeover bid when Shindongbang and Korea Industrial Co told the exchange they were considering taking over the retailer.
The presidents of Korea Industrial and Shindongbang are brothers.
Asked if the latest purchase was part of a plan to take over Midopa, the company spokesman declined to comment.
